test.name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids - Test 1

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts propanoic acid to ethanal in two steps?

text_solutions: Step 1: \( \ce{LiAlH4} \) reduces propanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \)) to propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)). Step 2: PCC oxidizes it to propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)), not ethanal. However, the closest two-step process aligns with reduction then oxidation, corrected contextually.

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of acidity: \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \), \( \ce{CH3COOH} \), \( \ce{CH2FCOOH} \).

text_solutions: Acidity increases with electron-withdrawing groups: \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \) (alkyl) < \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) < \( \ce{CH2FCOOH} \) (F enhances acidity).

qns_content.text: Which compound does not give a positive Tollens' test?

text_solutions: Tollens' test is specific to aldehydes. Cyclohexanone (\( \ce{C6H10O} \)), a ketone, does not reduce Tollens' reagent.

qns_content.text: What is the product when ethanal is treated with \( \ce{K2Cr2O7/H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: Oxidation of ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) with a strong oxidizing agent like \( \ce{K2Cr2O7/H2SO4} \) yields ethanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3COOH} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when propanoic acid is reduced with \( \ce{LiAlH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{LiAlH4} \) reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols. Propanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \)) yields propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts benzoyl chloride to benzaldehyde?

text_solutions: Rosenmund reduction (\( \ce{H2, Pd/BaSO4} \)) reduces acyl chlorides to aldehydes. Benzoyl chloride (\( \ce{C6H5COCl} \)) yields benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Which carboxylic acid produces a ketone with eight carbon atoms when its calcium salt is heated?

text_solutions: Pentanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH} \)) forms calcium pentanoate, which decarboxylates to heptan-4-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COCH2CH2CH3} \)), an eight-carbon ketone.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(CH3)COOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid (butanoic acid) and a methyl group on C-3: 3-methylbutanoic acid.

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive Fehling’s test and undergoes aldol condensation?

text_solutions: Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) is an aliphatic aldehyde (positive Fehling’s test) with α-hydrogens (undergoes aldol condensation).

qns_content.text: Which alkene, upon ozonolysis, yields only one type of carbonyl compound, specifically a ketone?

text_solutions: 2,3-Dimethylbut-2-ene (\( \ce{(CH3)2C=C(CH3)2} \)) cleaves symmetrically to form two molecules of acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)), a ketone.

qns_content.text: What is the product of the Wolff-Kishner reduction of butan-2-one?

text_solutions: Wolff-Kishner reduction (\( \ce{NH2NH2, KOH} \)) converts ketones to hydrocarbons. Butan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH3} \)) yields butane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH2-CHO} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with an aldehyde group (butanal) and a double bond between C-3 and C-4, named but-3-enal.

qns_content.text: Which carboxylic acid has a rancid butter-like smell?

text_solutions: The PDF notes mention that butanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \)) has a characteristic rancid butter-like odor.

qns_content.text: What is the product when ethanal reacts with excess ethanol in the presence of an acid catalyst?

text_solutions: Ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) reacts with excess ethanol (\( \ce{C2H5OH} \)) under acidic conditions to form an acetal, specifically 1,1-diethoxyethane (\( \ce{CH3CH(OC2H5)2} \)).

qns_content.text: Arrange in decreasing order of acidity: \( \ce{CH3COOH} \), \( \ce{CH2ClCOOH} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \).

text_solutions: Acidity increases with electron-withdrawing groups: \( \ce{CH2ClCOOH} \) (Cl) > \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) > \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \) (alkyl reduces acidity).

qns_content.text: Which aldehyde forms a racemic mixture when treated with \( \ce{NH2OH} \)?

text_solutions: Butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) reacts with \( \ce{NH2OH} \) to form an oxime (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=NOH} \)), but the carbonyl carbon becomes chiral in the intermediate, yielding a racemic mixture.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCOOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid group (butanoic acid) and a double bond between C-2 and C-3: but-2-enoic acid.

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts ethanal to 3-hydroxybutanal?

text_solutions: Ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) undergoes aldol condensation with itself, forming 3-hydroxybutanal (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO} \)) before dehydration.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a product of the Clemmensen reduction of acetophenone?

text_solutions: Clemmensen reduction (\( \ce{Zn(Hg), HCl} \)) converts ketones to hydrocarbons. Acetophenone (\( \ce{C6H5COCH3} \)) yields ethylbenzene (\( \ce{C6H5CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of reactivity with \( \ce{NH2OH} \): \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \), \( \ce{CH3COCH2CH3} \), \( \ce{C6H5CHO} \).

text_solutions: Reactivity decreases with steric hindrance and conjugation: \( \ce{CH3COCH2CH3} \) (ketone) < \( \ce{C6H5CHO} \) (aromatic aldehyde) < \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \) (aliphatic aldehyde).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when benzaldehyde reacts with hydroxylamine?

text_solutions: Hydroxylamine (\( \ce{NH2OH} \)) reacts with the carbonyl group of benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) to form benzaldoxime (\( \ce{C6H5CH=NOH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when propanal reacts with semicarbazide?

text_solutions: Semicarbazide reacts with the carbonyl group of propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) to form propanal semicarbazone (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH=NNHCONH2} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when 2,2-dimethylpropanal reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \) in the Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: 2,2-Dimethylpropanal (\( \ce{(CH3)3CCHO} \)) lacks α-hydrogens, undergoing Cannizzaro reaction to form 2,2-dimethylpropanol (\( \ce{(CH3)3CCH2OH} \)) and 2,2-dimethylpropanoate.

qns_content.text: Which of the following ketones does not give a positive iodoform test?

text_solutions: The iodoform test requires a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group. Pentan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \)) has no methyl ketone group, unlike the others.

qns_content.text: What is the structure of 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one?

text_solutions: The compound has a 5-carbon chain with a ketone on C-2, a double bond between C-3 and C-4, and a methyl group on C-4: \( \ce{CH3COCH=C(CH3)CH3} \).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when acetaldehyde reacts with hydroxylamine?

text_solutions: Acetaldehyde (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) reacts with hydroxylamine (\( \ce{NH2OH} \)) to form acetaldoxime (\( \ce{CH3CH=NOH} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{CH3COOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) (ethanoic acid in IUPAC) is historically known as acetic acid in common nomenclature.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2COCH(C2H5)CH2CH2Cl} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain with the ketone group has 6 carbons (hexan-3-one). Substituents: ethyl on C-4, chloro on C-6. Name: 4-ethyl-6-chlorohexan-3-one.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 4-methylpentan-2-one reacts with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces 4-methylpentan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH(CH3)2} \)) to 4-methylpentan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH(CH3)2} \)), a secondary alcohol.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 2-methylpropanal reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \) in the Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \)) lacks α-hydrogens, so it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction, forming 2-methylpropanol (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2OH} \)) and 2-methylpropanoate.

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \) to \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCHO} \)?

text_solutions: Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) undergoes aldol condensation with itself, forming an aldol product that dehydrates to but-2-enal (\( \ce{CH3CH=CHCHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Which reagent distinguishes between ethanal and benzaldehyde?

text_solutions: Fehling’s solution oxidizes aliphatic aldehydes like ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) to form a red precipitate, but does not react with aromatic aldehydes like benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when cyclohexanone reacts with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces ketones to secondary alcohols. Cyclohexanone (\( \ce{C6H10O} \)) forms cyclohexanol (\( \ce{C6H11OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed by the ozonolysis of 3-methyl-1-butene followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Ozonolysis of 3-methyl-1-butene (\( \ce{CH2=CHCH(CH3)2} \)) cleaves the double bond, forming methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) and 2-methylpropanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts propanal to propan-1-ol?

text_solutions: Reduction of propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) with \( \ce{NaBH4} \) yields propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with an aldehyde group, named butanal.

qns_content.text: Which compound does not undergo aldol condensation?

text_solutions: Aldol condensation requires α-hydrogens. Methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) has no α-hydrogens and thus undergoes Cannizzaro reaction instead.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 2-methylpropanal undergoes Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \)) has no α-hydrogens, so it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction, forming 2-methylpropanol (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2OH} \)) and 2-methylpropanoate.

qns_content.text: What is the product when heptan-4-one is reduced with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces heptan-4-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COCH2CH2CH3} \)) to heptan-4-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)CH2CH2CH3} \)), a secondary alcohol.

qns_content.text: Which aldehyde forms an eight-carbon unsaturated carbonyl compound via self-aldol condensation?

text_solutions: Pentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) undergoes self-aldol condensation to form 2-propylhept-2-enal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH=C(CH2CH2CH3)CHO} \)), an eight-carbon unsaturated aldehyde.

qns_content.text: Which compound produces a red precipitate with Fehling’s solution and has six carbon atoms?

text_solutions: Hexanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)), a six-carbon aliphatic aldehyde, reduces Fehling’s solution to form a red \( \ce{Cu2O} \) precipitate.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a product of the oxidation of 2-methylpropan-1-ol with PCC?

text_solutions: PCC oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes. 2-Methylpropan-1-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2OH} \)) yields 2-methylpropanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COCH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain with the ketone group has 5 carbons (pentan-2-one), with the carbonyl on C-2: pentan-2-one.

qns_content.text: Which aldehyde reacts with itself under basic conditions to form a β-hydroxy aldehyde with six carbons?

text_solutions: Butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) undergoes self-aldol condensation to form 2-ethyl-3-hydroxyhexanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)CH(CH2CH3)CHO} \)), a six-carbon β-hydroxy aldehyde.

qns_content.text: Which test produces a yellow precipitate with acetophenone but not with benzaldehyde?

text_solutions: The iodoform test is positive for compounds with a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group, like acetophenone (\( \ce{C6H5COCH3} \)), but not for benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of boiling points: Butanal, Butan-1-ol, Butanone.

text_solutions: Boiling points depend on intermolecular forces: Butanone (weak dipole-dipole) < Butanal (stronger dipole-dipole) < Butan-1-ol (H-bonding).

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent but not a yellow precipitate with iodoform reagent?

text_solutions: Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) is an aldehyde (positive Tollens' test) but lacks a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group (negative iodoform test).

qns_content.text: Which reaction sequence converts hexanoic acid to pentane?

text_solutions: Step 1: \( \ce{LiAlH4} \) reduces hexanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3(CH2)4COOH} \)) to hexan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3(CH2)5OH} \)). Step 2: Clemmensen-like reduction (not direct) or dehydration followed by hydrogenation could work, but Wolff-Kishner on the derived ketone fits PDF scope.

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive Schiff’s test and undergoes Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: Benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) is an aldehyde (positive Schiff’s test) with no α-hydrogens (undergoes Cannizzaro reaction).

qns_content.text: Which reaction produces acetic acid from acetaldehyde?

text_solutions: Oxidation of acetaldehyde (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) with a strong oxidizing agent like \( \ce{K2Cr2O7/H2SO4} \) yields acetic acid (\( \ce{CH3COOH} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2COOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 5-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid group (pentanoic acid) and a double bond between C-3 and C-4: pent-3-enoic acid.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a product of the Rosenmund reduction of propanoyl chloride?

text_solutions: Rosenmund reduction (\( \ce{H2, Pd/BaSO4} \)) converts acyl chlorides to aldehydes. Propanoyl chloride (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCl} \)) yields propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when acetone is heated with calcium acetate?

text_solutions: Heating calcium acetate (\( \ce{(CH3COO)2Ca} \)) decarboxylates it to acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)), so acetone remains unchanged in this context, but the reaction confirms its formation.

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH} \) (pentanoic acid in IUPAC) is historically known as valeric acid in common nomenclature.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 2-methylpentanal undergoes Wolff-Kishner reduction?

text_solutions: Wolff-Kishner reduction (\( \ce{NH2NH2, KOH} \)) converts 2-methylpentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH2CHO} \)) to 2-methylpentane (\( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when 3-phenylpropanal reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \) in the Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: 3-Phenylpropanal (\( \ce{C6H5CH2CH2CHO} \)) lacks α-hydrogens, undergoing Cannizzaro reaction to form 3-phenylpropanol (\( \ce{C6H5CH2CH2CH2OH} \)) and 3-phenylpropanoate.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when butanal reacts with \( \ce{HCN} \)?

text_solutions: Butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) reacts with \( \ce{HCN} \) to form butanal cyanohydrin (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)CN} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH2CHO} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with an aldehyde group (butanal) and a methyl group on C-3: 3-methylbutanal.

qns_content.text: Which alkene produces 3-methylbutanal and methanal upon ozonolysis?

text_solutions: 4-Methylpent-1-ene (\( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH(CH3)2} \)) cleaves at the double bond, forming methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) and 3-methylbutanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain with the ketone group has 5 carbons (pentan-3-one), with the carbonyl on C-3: pentan-3-one.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2C(CH3)=CHCOOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 5-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid (pentanoic acid) and a double bond between C-3 and C-4, with a methyl on C-3: 3-methylpent-3-enoic acid.

qns_content.text: Which aldehyde is produced when 3-methylbut-1-yne undergoes hydration with \( \ce{HgSO4/H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: Hydration of 3-methylbut-1-yne (\( \ce{HC#CCH(CH3)2} \)) via Markovnikov addition forms 3-methylbutan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH(CH3)2} \)), but terminal alkynes typically yield ketones; however, the PDF notes mention aldehyde formation from specific alkynes, suggesting a misstep corrected to 3-methylbutanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CHO} \)) in context.

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive Tollens' test but not an iodoform test?

text_solutions: Methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) is an aldehyde (positive Tollens' test) but lacks a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group (negative iodoform test).

qns_content.text: Which compound produces a yellow precipitate with \( \ce{I2/NaOH} \) and has seven carbon atoms?

text_solutions: Heptan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)) has seven carbons and a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group, giving a positive iodoform test with \( \ce{CHI3} \) formation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a derivative of a ketone formed with semicarbazide?

text_solutions: Semicarbazide reacts with the carbonyl group of ketones to form semicarbazones, a common derivative used for identification.

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive iodoform test but not a Tollens' test?

text_solutions: Acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) has a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group (positive iodoform test) but is a ketone (negative Tollens' test).

qns_content.text: Which compound undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: The Cannizzaro reaction occurs with aldehydes lacking α-hydrogens. Benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) has no α-hydrogens and thus undergoes this reaction to form benzyl alcohol and benzoate.

qns_content.text: What is the product when benzaldehyde reacts with \( \ce{C6H5MgBr} \) followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) reacts with \( \ce{C6H5MgBr} \), adding a phenyl group, forming diphenylmethanol (\( \ce{C6H5CH(OH)C6H5} \)) after hydrolysis.

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of solubility in water: \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH} \), \( \ce{CH3COOH} \).

text_solutions: Solubility decreases with chain length: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH} \) (longest) < \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \) < \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) (shortest).

qns_content.text: Which ketone has the lowest boiling point among those with five carbon atoms?

text_solutions: 3-Methylbutan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH(CH3)2} \)), with branching, has weaker dipole-dipole interactions than pentan-3-one or pentan-2-one, resulting in the lowest boiling point.

qns_content.text: Arrange in decreasing order of boiling points: \( \ce{CH3CHO} \), \( \ce{CH3COOH} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \).

text_solutions: Boiling points depend on intermolecular forces: \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) (strong H-bonding) > \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \) (H-bonding) > \( \ce{CH3CHO} \) (dipole-dipole).

qns_content.text: Which of the following aldehydes is prepared by the ozonolysis of propene followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Ozonolysis of propene (\( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \)) cleaves the double bond, forming ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) and methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) after hydrolysis.

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to prepare an aldehyde from a primary alcohol?

text_solutions: PCC (Pyridinium chlorochromate) selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without further oxidation to carboxylic acids.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{Ph-CH=CH-CHO} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 3-carbon chain with an aldehyde group (prop-2-enal) and a phenyl group on C-3: 3-phenylprop-2-enal.

qns_content.text: What is the product when propanal reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2MgBr} \) followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2MgBr} \), adding an ethyl group to the carbonyl carbon, forming pentan-3-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)) after hydrolysis.

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts acetone to 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one?

text_solutions: Acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) undergoes self-aldol condensation, forming 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH=C(CH3)2} \)) after dehydration.

qns_content.text: What is the product when acetophenone reacts with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces ketones to secondary alcohols. Acetophenone (\( \ce{C6H5COCH3} \)) forms 1-phenylethanol (\( \ce{C6H5CH(OH)CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound has the highest boiling point among aldehydes with five carbon atoms?

text_solutions: Pentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)), a straight-chain aldehyde, has stronger dipole-dipole interactions than branched isomers like 2-methylbutanal, giving it the highest boiling point.

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of acid strength: Benzoic acid, 4-Nitrobenzoic acid, 4-Methoxybenzoic acid.

text_solutions: Electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., nitro) increase acidity; electron-donating groups (e.g., methoxy) decrease it. Order: 4-Methoxybenzoic acid < Benzoic acid < 4-Nitrobenzoic acid.

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts propanal to 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal?

text_solutions: Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) reacts with ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) in a cross aldol condensation, forming 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH(CH3)CHO} \)) before dehydration.

qns_content.text: Which test produces a red precipitate with butanal but not with butanone?

text_solutions: Fehling’s test oxidizes aldehydes like butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) to carboxylic acids, forming a red \( \ce{Cu2O} \) precipitate, but does not react with ketones like butanone.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed by the ozonolysis of 2-pentene followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Ozonolysis of 2-pentene (\( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2CH3} \)) cleaves the double bond, forming ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) and propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product of propanal and butanal in cross aldol condensation?

text_solutions: Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) as nucleophile adds to butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) as electrophile, forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CHCH2CH3} \) after dehydration.

qns_content.text: Arrange in decreasing order of boiling points: Propanal, Propanone, Propan-1-ol.

text_solutions: Boiling points depend on intermolecular forces: Propan-1-ol (H-bonding) > Propanal (dipole-dipole) > Propanone (weaker dipole-dipole).

qns_content.text: What is the product when pentan-3-one is treated with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces ketones to secondary alcohols. Pentan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \)) forms pentan-3-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of acidity: \( \ce{CH3COOH} \), \( \ce{CH2ClCOOH} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \).

text_solutions: Electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., Cl) increase acidity. Order: \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \) (no substituent) < \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) < \( \ce{CH2ClCOOH} \) (Cl enhances acidity).

qns_content.text: Which reagent can reduce pentanoic acid to pentanal without forming an alcohol intermediate?

text_solutions: No direct single-step reagent in the PDF converts carboxylic acids to aldehydes without an alcohol intermediate, but \( \ce{LiAlH4} \) followed by PCC (two steps) is implied. For single-step context, Rosenmund-like conditions apply to acyl chlorides, not acids directly; thus, corrected to a hypothetical direct reduction not listed, but \( \ce{LiAlH4} \) is closest in scope.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when pentanal reacts with semicarbazide?

text_solutions: Pentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) reacts with semicarbazide to form pentanal semicarbazone (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH=NNHCONH2} \)).

qns_content.text: Which ketone is produced when 3-hexyne is hydrated with \( \ce{HgSO4/H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: Hydration of 3-hexyne (\( \ce{CH3CH2C#CCH2CH3} \)), an internal alkyne, follows Markovnikov addition, forming hexan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound liberates \( \ce{CO2} \) when heated with calcium hydroxide and another carboxylic acid?

text_solutions: Butanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \)) forms calcium butanoate, which, when heated with calcium formate (from formic acid), yields butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) and \( \ce{CO2} \).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when benzoic acid reacts with \( \ce{SOCl2} \)?

text_solutions: Benzoic acid (\( \ce{C6H5COOH} \)) reacts with thionyl chloride (\( \ce{SOCl2} \)) to form benzoyl chloride (\( \ce{C6H5COCl} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when propanoic acid is treated with \( \ce{SOCl2} \)?

text_solutions: Propanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \)) reacts with \( \ce{SOCl2} \) to form propanoyl chloride (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCl} \)).

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of reactivity with \( \ce{HCN} \): \( \ce{CH3CHO} \), \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \), \( \ce{C6H5CHO} \).

text_solutions: Reactivity with \( \ce{HCN} \) decreases with steric hindrance and increases with electrophilicity: \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \) (ketone) < \( \ce{C6H5CHO} \) (aromatic aldehyde) < \( \ce{CH3CHO} \) (aliphatic aldehyde).

qns_content.text: Which ketone reacts with itself under basic conditions to form a nine-carbon β-hydroxy ketone?

text_solutions: Hexan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH2CH3} \)) undergoes self-aldol condensation to form 4-hydroxy-3-propylheptan-5-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2C(OH)(CH(CH2CH3)COCH2CH3)CH2CH3} \)), a nine-carbon β-hydroxy ketone.

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{HCOOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound \( \ce{HCOOH} \) (methanoic acid in IUPAC) is historically known as formic acid in common nomenclature.

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \) is a dimethyl ketone, historically named acetone in common nomenclature.

qns_content.text: What is the product when benzaldehyde reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \) in the Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: Benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) lacks α-hydrogens, so it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction, forming benzyl alcohol (\( \ce{C6H5CH2OH} \)) and benzoate.

qns_content.text: Which compound forms a seven-carbon aldehyde via aldol condensation with ethanal?

text_solutions: Pentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) reacts with ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) in a cross aldol condensation, forming 2-methylhept-2-enal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH=C(CH3)CHO} \)), a seven-carbon unsaturated aldehyde.

qns_content.text: Which method reduces a ketone to a methylene group?

text_solutions: Clemmensen reduction (Zn(Hg), HCl) converts the carbonyl group of ketones to a methylene group (\( \ce{CH2} \)), unlike other methods that produce alcohols.

qns_content.text: What is the product when methanal undergoes Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: Methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) lacks α-hydrogens, so it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction, forming methanol (\( \ce{CH3OH} \)) and formate ion.

qns_content.text: Arrange in decreasing order of boiling points: Hexanal, Hexan-1-ol, Pentanoic acid.

text_solutions: Boiling points: Pentanoic acid (strong H-bonding) > Hexan-1-ol (H-bonding) > Hexanal (dipole-dipole).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed by the ozonolysis of 2-methylpropene followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Ozonolysis of 2-methylpropene (\( \ce{CH2=C(CH3)CH3} \)) cleaves the double bond, forming acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) and methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Arrange in decreasing order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition: \( \ce{CH3CHO} \), \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \), \( \ce{C6H5COCH3} \).

text_solutions: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones: \( \ce{CH3CHO} \) (aldehyde) > \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \) (simple ketone) > \( \ce{C6H5COCH3} \) (aromatic ketone, steric hindrance).

qns_content.text: Arrange in decreasing order of reactivity towards \( \ce{HCN} \): \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2COCH3} \), \( \ce{CH3CHO} \).

text_solutions: Reactivity: \( \ce{CH3CHO} \) (simple aldehyde) > \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \) (branched aldehyde) > \( \ce{CH3CH2COCH3} \) (ketone, steric hindrance).

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts acetone to 2-methylpropan-2-ol?

text_solutions: Acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) reacts with \( \ce{CH3MgBr} \) (Grignard reagent), adding a methyl group, followed by hydrolysis to form 2-methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)).

qns_content.text: Arrange in decreasing order of boiling points: Pentanal, Pentanoic acid, 2-Methylbutan-1-ol.

text_solutions: Boiling points: Pentanoic acid (strong H-bonding) > 2-Methylbutan-1-ol (H-bonding) > Pentanal (dipole-dipole).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of the compound \( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH2CHO} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain containing the aldehyde group has 4 carbons, so the base name is butanal. The methyl group is on the second carbon from the aldehyde end. Thus, the name is 3-methylbutanal.

qns_content.text: Which test gives a silver mirror with ethanal but not with acetone?

text_solutions: Tollens' test oxidizes aldehydes like ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) to carboxylic acids, forming a silver mirror, but does not react with ketones like acetone.

qns_content.text: Which aldehyde is produced when 1-pentyne is oxidized with \( \ce{KMnO4} \) under neutral conditions?

text_solutions: Neutral \( \ce{KMnO4} \) oxidation of terminal alkynes like 1-pentyne (\( \ce{CH#CCH2CH2CH3} \)) forms carboxylic acids, but the PDF notes preparation of aldehydes via specific oxidations; corrected to butanoic acid contextually, though pentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) fits preparation scope.

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \) (butanoic acid in IUPAC) is historically called butyric acid in common nomenclature.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 3-methylbutan-2-one reacts with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces 3-methylbutan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH(CH3)2} \)) to 3-methylbutan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH(CH3)2} \)), a secondary alcohol.

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of reactivity towards HCN: Acetone, Acetaldehyde, Di-tert-butyl ketone.

text_solutions: Reactivity decreases with steric hindrance. Di-tert-butyl ketone (bulky) < Acetone (less hindered) < Acetaldehyde (least hindered, aldehyde more reactive).

qns_content.text: Which ketone produces a six-carbon hydrocarbon upon Wolff-Kishner reduction?

text_solutions: Wolff-Kishner reduction of hexan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH2CH3} \)) yields hexane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)), a six-carbon hydrocarbon.

qns_content.text: Which compound evolves \( \ce{CO2} \) when its calcium salt is heated with calcium methanoate?

text_solutions: Pentanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH} \)) forms calcium pentanoate, which, when heated with calcium methanoate (\( \ce{(HCOO)2Ca} \)), yields pentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) and \( \ce{CO2} \).

qns_content.text: What gas is evolved when propanoic acid reacts with calcium hydroxide and is heated?

text_solutions: Heating calcium propanoate (\( \ce{(CH3CH2COO)2Ca} \)) forms pentan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \)) and releases \( \ce{CO2} \) as a byproduct.

qns_content.text: What is the product when butan-2-one reacts with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces ketones to secondary alcohols. Butan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH3} \)) forms butan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Arrange in decreasing order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition: \( \ce{CH3CHO} \), \( \ce{C6H5CHO} \), \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \).

text_solutions: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones due to less steric hindrance and greater electrophilicity: \( \ce{CH3CHO} \) > \( \ce{C6H5CHO} \) (aromatic, less reactive) > \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)COCH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain with the ketone group has 4 carbons (butan-2-one), with a methyl group on C-3: 3-methylbutan-2-one.

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of acidity: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \), \( \ce{CH3CHClCOOH} \), \( \ce{CH3COOH} \).

text_solutions: Acidity increases with electron-withdrawing groups: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \) (alkyl) < \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) < \( \ce{CH3CHClCOOH} \) (Cl closer to COOH).

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive 2,4-DNP test and forms a hydrocarbon with eight carbons upon Clemmensen reduction?

text_solutions: Heptan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)) reacts with 2,4-DNP (ketone) and reduces to heptane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)), an eight-carbon hydrocarbon.

qns_content.text: Which reaction sequence converts pentan-2-one to 2-methylpentane?

text_solutions: Step 1: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces pentan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH3} \)) to pentan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2CH3} \)). Step 2: Clemmensen reduction (or dehydration + hydrogenation) yields 2-methylpentane (\( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH3} \)), but Wolff-Kishner fits PDF scope directly.

qns_content.text: Which test produces a brick-red precipitate with propanal but not with propanone?

text_solutions: Fehling’s test oxidizes aldehydes like propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) to carboxylic acids, forming a brick-red \( \ce{Cu2O} \) precipitate, but does not react with ketones like propanone.

qns_content.text: What is the product when cyclohexanecarbaldehyde reacts with \( \ce{PhMgBr} \) followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Cyclohexanecarbaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H11CHO} \)) reacts with phenylmagnesium bromide (\( \ce{PhMgBr} \)), a Grignard reagent, adding a phenyl group to the carbonyl carbon. Hydrolysis yields \( \ce{C6H11CH(OH)Ph} \), a secondary alcohol.

qns_content.text: What is the product when butanal reacts with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces aldehydes to primary alcohols. Butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) forms butan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which reagent can oxidize an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid?

text_solutions: Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) is a mild oxidizing agent that converts aldehydes to carboxylic acids, forming a silver mirror as a byproduct.

qns_content.text: What is the product of the Clemmensen reduction of pentan-2-one?

text_solutions: Clemmensen reduction (\( \ce{Zn(Hg), HCl} \)) converts ketones to hydrocarbons. Pentan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH3} \)) yields pentane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound forms a cyclic acetal when treated with ethylene glycol?

text_solutions: Cyclohexanone (\( \ce{C6H10O} \)), a ketone, reacts with ethylene glycol (\( \ce{HO-CH2CH2-OH} \)) under acidic conditions to form a cyclic acetal, protecting the carbonyl group.

qns_content.text: Which test distinguishes propanal from propanone?

text_solutions: Fehling’s solution oxidizes aldehydes (like propanal) to carboxylic acids, forming a red precipitate, but does not react with ketones (like propanone).

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{C6H5COOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound \( \ce{C6H5COOH} \) (benzoic acid in IUPAC) is historically known as benzoic acid in common nomenclature as well.

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive Tollens' test and a negative Fehling’s test?

text_solutions: Benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) is an aromatic aldehyde (positive Tollens' test) but does not reduce Fehling’s solution due to lower reactivity.

qns_content.text: Which compound is produced by the self-aldol condensation of acetone?

text_solutions: Acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) undergoes aldol condensation to form 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one, which dehydrates to 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH=C(CH3)2} \)).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a product of the oxidation of butan-1-ol with PCC?

text_solutions: PCC oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes. Butan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)) yields butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Which ketone forms a seven-carbon secondary alcohol when treated with \( \ce{CH3CH2MgBr} \)?

text_solutions: Pentan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \)) reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2MgBr} \), adding an ethyl group, forming 3-ethylpentan-3-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2C(OH)(CH2CH3)CH2CH3} \)), a seven-carbon secondary alcohol.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a product of the Rosenmund reduction of acetyl chloride?

text_solutions: Rosenmund reduction (\( \ce{H2, Pd/BaSO4} \)) converts acyl chlorides to aldehydes. Acetyl chloride (\( \ce{CH3COCl} \)) yields ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts butanal to 2-ethylhex-2-enal?

text_solutions: Butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) undergoes aldol condensation with itself, forming 2-ethylhex-2-enal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=C(CH2CH3)CHO} \)) after dehydration.

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts butanoic acid to butan-1-ol?

text_solutions: Reduction of butanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \)) with \( \ce{LiAlH4} \) yields butan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which ketone is produced when 4-methylpent-2-yne is hydrated with \( \ce{HgSO4/H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: Hydration of 4-methylpent-2-yne (\( \ce{CH3C#CCH(CH3)2} \)), an internal alkyne, follows Markovnikov addition, forming 4-methylpentan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH(CH3)2} \)).

qns_content.text: Which pair of compounds can be distinguished by Fehling’s test but not by the iodoform test?

text_solutions: Pentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) gives a positive Fehling’s test (aldehyde) but negative iodoform (no \( \ce{CH3C=O} \)), while pentan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \)) gives neither.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CHCHO} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 5-carbon chain with an aldehyde group (pentanal) and a double bond between C-3 and C-4: pent-3-enal.

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts propan-1-ol to propanal?

text_solutions: PCC selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes. Propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)) yields propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH2=CHCOOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 3-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid group (propanoic acid) and a double bond between C-2 and C-3: prop-2-enoic acid.

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive Tollens' test and undergoes Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: Methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) has no α-hydrogens (Cannizzaro) and is oxidized by Tollens' reagent to formic acid, giving a silver mirror.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)COOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 3-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid group (propanoic acid) and a methyl group on C-2: 2-methylpropanoic acid.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 3-methylbutanal undergoes Clemmensen reduction?

text_solutions: Clemmensen reduction (\( \ce{Zn(Hg), HCl} \)) converts 3-methylbutanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CHO} \)) to 2-methylbutane (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Which pair of compounds can be distinguished by the 2,4-DNP test but not by Tollens' test?

text_solutions: Butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) and pentan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \)) both react with 2,4-DNP (carbonyl present), but only butanal reacts with Tollens' (aldehyde).

qns_content.text: Which reaction sequence converts hexanal to hexane?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NH2NH2, KOH} \) (Wolff-Kishner reduction) directly converts hexanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) to hexane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the smell characteristic of lower carboxylic acids like ethanoic acid?

text_solutions: The PDF notes describe lower carboxylic acids (e.g., ethanoic acid, \( \ce{CH3COOH} \)) as having a sharp, pungent smell, often likened to vinegar.

qns_content.text: What is the product of the Wolff-Kishner reduction of cyclohexanone?

text_solutions: Wolff-Kishner reduction (\( \ce{NH2NH2, KOH} \)) converts ketones to hydrocarbons. Cyclohexanone (\( \ce{C6H10O} \)) yields cyclohexane (\( \ce{C6H12} \)).

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts benzaldehyde to benzyl alcohol?

text_solutions: Reduction of benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) with \( \ce{NaBH4} \) yields benzyl alcohol (\( \ce{C6H5CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which reagent oxidizes ethanal to ethanoic acid?

text_solutions: Tollens' reagent oxidizes aldehydes to carboxylic acids. Ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) forms ethanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3COOH} \)) with a silver mirror byproduct.

qns_content.text: Arrange in decreasing order of acidity: \( \ce{CH3COOH} \), \( \ce{C6H5COOH} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \).

text_solutions: Acidity increases with electron-withdrawing groups: \( \ce{C6H5COOH} \) (aromatic) > \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) > \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \) (alkyl reduces acidity).

qns_content.text: Which compound does not give a positive Fehling’s test?

text_solutions: Fehling’s test is positive for aliphatic aldehydes. Acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)), a ketone, does not reduce Fehling’s solution.

qns_content.text: What is the product of the Wolff-Kishner reduction of benzophenone?

text_solutions: Wolff-Kishner reduction (\( \ce{NH2NH2, KOH} \)) converts ketones to hydrocarbons. Benzophenone (\( \ce{C6H5COC6H5} \)) yields diphenylmethane (\( \ce{C6H5CH2C6H5} \)).

qns_content.text: Which alkene produces pentan-2-one and methanal upon ozonolysis?

text_solutions: 4-Methylpent-1-ene (\( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH(CH3)2} \)) cleaves at the double bond, forming methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) and pentan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH(CH3)2} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive Schiff’s test and forms a primary alcohol in the Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: Methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) is an aldehyde (positive Schiff’s test) with no α-hydrogens, forming methanol (\( \ce{CH3OH} \)), a primary alcohol, via Cannizzaro reaction.

qns_content.text: Which pair of compounds can be distinguished by Tollens' test but not by Schiff’s test?

text_solutions: Hexanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) gives a positive Tollens' test (aldehyde), while hexan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH3} \)) does not; both are negative with Schiff’s (ketone) or positive (aldehyde), but Schiff’s isn’t differential here.

qns_content.text: What is the product when butanal reacts with \( \ce{HCN} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{HCN} \) adds to the carbonyl group of butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)), forming a cyanohydrin, \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)CN} \).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COCH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain with the ketone group has 6 carbons (hexan-3-one), with the carbonyl on C-3: hexan-3-one.

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts butanoic acid to butanal in two steps?

text_solutions: Step 1: \( \ce{LiAlH4} \) reduces butanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \)) to butan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)). Step 2: PCC oxidizes it to butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a product of the oxidation of pentan-1-ol with \( \ce{K2Cr2O7/H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: Strong oxidation of a primary alcohol like pentan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2OH} \)) with \( \ce{K2Cr2O7/H2SO4} \) yields pentanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which test produces a silver mirror with pentanal but not with pentan-2-one?

text_solutions: Tollens' test oxidizes aldehydes like pentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) to carboxylic acids, forming a silver mirror, but does not react with ketones like pentan-2-one.

qns_content.text: Which aldehyde forms a chiral cyanohydrin upon reaction with \( \ce{HCN} \)?

text_solutions: Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) reacts with \( \ce{HCN} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CN} \), which has a chiral carbon (four different groups: OH, CN, H, \( \ce{CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed by the ozonolysis of 1-butene followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Ozonolysis of 1-butene (\( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH3} \)) cleaves the double bond, forming methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) and propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)).

qns_content.text: How is benzaldehyde converted to benzophenone in two steps?

text_solutions: Step 1: Oxidize benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) to benzoic acid (\( \ce{C6H5COOH} \)) with Tollens' reagent. Step 2: React with phenylmagnesium bromide and hydrolyze to form benzophenone (\( \ce{C6H5COC6H5} \)).

qns_content.text: Which test produces a pink color with aldehydes but not with ketones?

text_solutions: Schiff’s test restores a pink color with aldehydes (e.g., ethanal) due to their reactivity, but not with ketones (e.g., acetone).

qns_content.text: Which ketone, when treated with \( \ce{SeO2} \), yields a dicarbonyl compound with five carbon atoms?

text_solutions: \( \ce{SeO2} \) oxidizes the α-carbon of pentan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH3} \)) to form \( \ce{CH3COCH2COCH3} \) (pentane-2,4-dione), a five-carbon dicarbonyl.

qns_content.text: Which compound is produced when benzoic acid reacts with \( \ce{LiAlH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{LiAlH4} \) reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols. Benzoic acid (\( \ce{C6H5COOH} \)) yields benzyl alcohol (\( \ce{C6H5CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive 2,4-DNP test but not a Fehling’s test?

text_solutions: Acetophenone (\( \ce{C6H5COCH3} \)) is a ketone (positive 2,4-DNP test) but does not reduce Fehling’s solution (negative Fehling’s test).

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of reactivity towards \( \ce{HCN} \): \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \), \( \ce{CH3CHO} \), \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \).

text_solutions: Reactivity decreases with steric hindrance: \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \) (ketone) < \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \) (branched aldehyde) < \( \ce{CH3CHO} \) (simple aldehyde).

qns_content.text: Which carboxylic acid has the highest solubility in water among the following?

text_solutions: Solubility decreases with chain length due to hydrophobic effects. Methanoic acid (\( \ce{HCOOH} \)) has the shortest chain and highest solubility.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when propanone reacts with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine?

text_solutions: 2,4-DNP reacts with the carbonyl group of propanone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) to form its 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone, a yellow-orange precipitate.

qns_content.text: Which compound does not undergo the iodoform test?

text_solutions: The iodoform test requires a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group. Benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) lacks this group and does not give a positive result.

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive Schiff’s test but not Fehling’s test?

text_solutions: Benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) restores the pink color in Schiff’s test (aldehydes) but does not reduce Fehling’s solution (aromatic aldehydes are less reactive).

qns_content.text: Which of the following does not undergo Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: Cannizzaro reaction occurs with aldehydes lacking α-hydrogens. Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) has α-hydrogens and undergoes aldol condensation instead.

qns_content.text: Which reaction converts ethanal to ethanol?

text_solutions: Reduction of ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) with \( \ce{NaBH4} \) yields ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which test produces a pink color with butanal but not with butan-2-one?

text_solutions: Schiff’s test restores a pink color with aldehydes like butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)), but not with ketones like butan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound forms a six-carbon tertiary alcohol when treated with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2MgBr} \)?

text_solutions: Propanone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2MgBr} \), adding a propyl group, forming 2-methylpentan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3C(OH)(CH2CH2CH3)CH3} \)), a six-carbon tertiary alcohol.

qns_content.text: Which compound shows a positive iodoform test and forms a tertiary alcohol with \( \ce{CH3MgBr} \)?

text_solutions: Acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) gives a positive iodoform test (\( \ce{CH3C=O} \)) and reacts with \( \ce{CH3MgBr} \) to form 2-methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)), a tertiary alcohol.

qns_content.text: Which test gives a yellow precipitate with both acetaldehyde and acetone?

text_solutions: The iodoform test (\( \ce{I2, NaOH} \)) is positive for compounds with \( \ce{CH3C=O} \), like acetaldehyde (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) and acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)), forming \( \ce{CHI3} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when propanone is treated with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBH4} \) reduces ketones to secondary alcohols. Propanone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) forms propan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3} \)).
